advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the library close_reason derivation on close_class (only pass reason as close_reason when target is closed and close_class is a reason-required administrative class), mirroring the CLI's _plain_reason_refused, or reject the mismatch in close_class_refusal.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:295: `close_reason=("" if (force or force_close) else reason),`

transition.py CLI guards this: `if _plain_reason_refused(reason, force, target_status, close_class):` (transition.py:578) which returns False (not refused) only when target=='closed' and close_class in REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES

txn.close_class_refusal only requires/validates a reason when `close_class in close_disposition.REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES`; it never rejects a stray close_reason on other classes (txn.py close_class_refusal body)
reducer folds any close_reason present: src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py `if data.get("status") == "closed" and data.get("close_reason"): state["close_reason"] = data["close_reason"]`
advisory.finding: The library transition() path persists close_reason for non-administrative closes that the CLI refuses: `close_reason=("" if (force or force_close) else reason)` is computed unconditionally of close_class, so a non-force library close with a reason and a non-reason-required class (e.g. a bug with --class=regression, or any close_class not in REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) will set close_reason on the STATUS event. The CLI blocks this via _plain_reason_refused, and close_class_refusal does not catch it because reason-required validation only fires for obsolete/wontfix.
scenarios: A library/API caller invokes rebar.transition(bug, in_progress, closed, close_class='regression', reason='some note') without force — close_reason='some note' is written to the close event and surfaces in `rebar show --output json` as close_reason, contrary to the documented 'reason-only administrative close' semantics and the CLI's own refusal.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _lib_writes.transition, restrict close_reason to reason-required administrative closes, e.g. compute it as reason only when not (force or force_close) and target_status=='closed' and close_class in close_disposition.REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES; otherwise ''. Alternatively have close_class_refusal reject a close_reason supplied with a class not in REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update or retire tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_reason_honest_3803.py::test_transition_core_has_no_close_reason_param (and its AC1 docstring), since fc20 intentionally re-adds close_reason to txn.transition_core.
evidence: Diff adds `close_reason: str = ","` to transition_core: `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:249: close_reason: str = "",`

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_reason_honest_3803.py:78-84: `def test_transition_core_has_no_close_reason_param() -> None: ... params = inspect.signature(txn.transition_core).parameters; assert "close_reason" not in params`
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_reason_honest_3803.py:12 (docstring AC1): `- AC1: ``close_reason`` is removed from ``transition_core``'s signature.`

This test file is NOT among the 17 changed files in the diff, so its assertion still runs against the new signature and will fail — an asymmetric interface change where the consumer (in-repo test asserting parameter absence) was not updated.
advisory.finding: Re-adding the `close_reason` parameter to `txn.transition_core` breaks the existing drift-guard test `test_transition_core_has_no_close_reason_param`, which asserts the parameter is absent from the signature; that test file was not updated in this change.
scenarios: CI runs the full interfaces suite; test_transition_reason_honest_3803.py::test_transition_core_has_no_close_reason_param fails because close_reason is now present in the signature.
advisory.suggested_fix: Since fc20 deliberately re-introduces close_reason (now actually persisted, not discarded), amend test_transition_reason_honest_3803.py: drop/rewrite test_transition_core_has_no_close_reason_param to assert the parameter now exists AND is persisted, and update the AC1 docstring to reflect the superseding fc20 contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for a forced reason-only close (`--class=obsolete --force=<reason>`): assert it is admitted (not refused), that reduced state records force_close_reason and NOT close_reason, and that the close is force-bypassed (unsigned).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:228 `if close_class in close_disposition.REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES and not (` / `close_reason or force_close_reason`
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:295 `close_reason=("" if (force or force_close) else reason),`

Absence: search of test_administrative_close_dispositions.py for `force=` returns only `--class=escalated --force=...` (refused) and `--force=just close it` (no class); no forced obsolete/wontfix case asserting success + close_reason absent + force_close_reason present.
advisory.finding: No test exercises a FORCED obsolete/wontfix close where --force=<reason> satisfies the reason requirement. txn.close_class_refusal added the branch `if close_class in REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES and not (close_reason or force_close_reason)`, so a `--class=obsolete --force=<reason>` close is admitted by the class guard specifically because the force reason substitutes for --reason; and _lib_writes.py suppresses close_reason on any forced close (`close_reason=("" if (force or force_close) else reason)`). The tests only cover a forced bug-only class (refused) and a forced no-class close (hint), never the admitted forced reason-only-class path.
scenarios: Operator runs `rebar transition <task> in_progress closed --class=obsolete --force="premise gone"` — the force reason satisfies the reason guard, close succeeds, but close_reason is intentionally not folded (recorded as force_close_reason instead).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `store`-based test closing a task with `--class=obsolete --force="premise gone"` asserting rc==0, `state["force_close_reason"]` present, `"close_reason" not in state`, and `state["status"]=="closed"`.
